caseStudyHeader.heading: Offering Content Reporting
caseStudyHeader.body: A dashboard for service offering teams that provides visibility into their offering's readiness and consultant usage.

summary.title: Outcome
summary.description: I delivered a high-fidelity prototype that articulated a new governance model and provided qualitative feedback for the first time.

summary.title: Goal
summary.description: The dashboard aimed to help service offering teams manage the lifecycle of their Offering and integrate them into a new content management system, Content+.

summary.title: Role
summary.description: I owned the reporting dashboard and my biggest contribution was building out its interface.

summary.title: Client and scope
summary.description: The internal client for this project was a cross-functional team representing IBM Services and lasted 4 months in 2020.

context.statement: How might we design a better way for offering team members to maintain quality offering content?
list: Consultants needed fresh, calibrated content for client opportunities, but what offering teams provided was often outdated or inconsistently maintained.
Offering teams lacked centralized, sufficient data to understand how their content was actually being used.
Offering teams lacked the incentives and feedback loops to prioritize improving their content over time.
The vision was to extend how teams manage their offering's lifecycle — tracking, strategizing, and evolving their content based on real feedback.

subsections.subhead: Offering teams receive alerts and use summaries to identify gaps in their offering content and organizational reach.
The report integrates with the offering profile to drive adoption of the dashboard and reduce mental models.

showcases.captionBody: Offering team members switch to the dashboard from the Offering Profile
The Offering Profile and Dashboard share layout and navigation patterns.

subsections.subhead: The report communicates rules set by governance and uses persuasive design patterns to stir up intrinsic motivators.

showcases.captionBody: Alerts drive Offering team members toward urgent actions that need resolution.
Offering teams will be motivated to be similar to or compete with their peers.

subsections.subhead: The report prioritizes showing conclusions first then providing evidence second using various visual design principles.
The report combines rich usage data and qualitative feedback to guide offering lifecycle activities in real time.

showcases.captionBody: Offering teams can understand how an artifact’s helpfulness is trending.
Sorely missing, Offering teams can start to understand the underlying reasons for their content’s performance.

list: Offering teams had no view of how their content was used or valued
I led research that surfaced who updates offering content and why
I designed an alert-based dashboard that nudges teams to resolve outdated content
I delivered a feedback loop that shows teams the organization’s sentiment
